policy.statement: Obus may autonomously propose, isolate, evaluate, reject, monitor, and roll back candidate improvements. It may never alter its evaluator or held-out suite, inspect held-out answers, expand its own authority, or authorize its own production promotion.
policy.purpose: Make improvement evidence reproducible and rollback-ready without treating self-judgment, runtime warmth, or benchmark optimization as proof of general capability.

source_supported_methods.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
source_supported_methods.supports: Documented and repeatable testing, independent assessment, monitoring, residual-risk decisions, and safe deactivation.

source_supported_methods.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework 1.1
source_supported_methods.supports: A secure development lifecycle, prevention of recurring vulnerabilities, and verifiable practices.

source_supported_methods.title: SLSA Provenance v1.1
source_supported_methods.supports: Content-addressed artifacts and verifiable build inputs, dependencies, builder identity, and outputs.

source_supported_methods.title: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
source_supported_methods.supports: Frozen held-out tasks and reproducible environments while warning that benchmark conditions do not represent all real work.

source_supported_methods.title: Spontaneous Reward Hacking in Iterative Self-Refinement
source_supported_methods.supports: Independent evaluation because iterative self-judging can improve a proxy while actual quality stagnates or declines.

source_supported_methods.title: OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2
source_supported_methods.supports: Separate capability and safeguard evidence plus an authorized review decision before high-risk deployment.

provenance_note: The sources support the control methods. Numeric thresholds and the exact authorization policy are normative Obus design choices, not claims attributed to those sources.
